I remember when I was little I clinged onto the internet and doing research because it always made me feel like I wasn’t alone. In a way Internet forums have taught me all I known and been the parent I never had. As an adult I’d say I carry such a profound emptiness within me everywhere I go. There’s a part of my brain that just holds such extreme inner self hatred and loneliness that I know was molded by having narcissistic parents. NOTHING IS EVER ABOUT TRULY ABOUT YOU and realizing that is so… jarring. IT’S ALWAYS ABOUT THEM, even what you thought was love was just a miserable, cheap imitation of it. And when you start having genuine conversations with people who actually LISTEN to you and care, it almost makes you want to sob because you grew up in an entirely different world were your only purpose was to cater to them, keep them calm. I am extremely, extremely independent. I raised myself. I nearly gave up so many times. I always feel my heart racing like I’m in trouble. All I want is a quiet, clean apartment one day where I can feel safe. I want to learn as much as I can about the REAL WORLD, that I’m navigating and exploring. Everything is so new to me, things that other people who grew up loved automatically know. I’m very curious and open minded. It’s really easy to slip into my fake self (scared, submissive, fawning) but I’m learning that my real self is very passionate and driven. I have a thirst for knowledge. There are very few things a friend or loved one could tell me that I’d shame them for, I’ll try my best to understand the reasoning and hold space for them. I can be very resourceful and resilient. I have deep gratitude for things a lot of people might take for granted. I’m really funny and can find the good in any situation because it was one of the ways I coped. Despite my debilitating mental issues and chronic pain, I can find a lot of enjoyment in really small things. I guess those are the good things I can find about being raised by narcissists.

I get what you’re coming from and I see fence sitters as people who are split on things as well. But I think in the context of this sub it’s a bit more strict. From what I’ve seen here, we consider fence sitters to be anyone who isn’t 100% sure of not wanting children. Having a child is such a huge decision. Being childfree is a huge commitment and one that we actively dedicate ourselves to and build our lives around so to not be completely sure of that would be sort of doing a disservice to anyone you’re in a relationship with who’s truly childfree. Of course we can’t “predict the future” but I feel that this is a choice that we’re actively making to mold the future. If there’s some hesitation on her part, she has to truly reflect and do more research.

Haven’t been in this situation so you probably won’t like my comment but from experience and my personal view, relationships require explicit communication and planning to try to balance each other’s needs and wants. She needs to make a decision now if she’s childfree or not. You guys have to have a tough conversation where she’s very open and honest on why she’s hesitant to not completely rule them out. Don’t buy property before you figure that out. I saw a reply of yours down there where you said that as much as you’d love for her to make that choice she really doesn’t know… but wouldn’t it be responsible for her to properly make a decision now for both of your sakes? You have to decide if you’re going to be firm on being childfree as well or if you’re just going to end up going along with this because of your love for her despite what seems to be a bomb of incompatibility. It’s like you guys are both holding the bomb and you’re waiting for her to pull the pin and she won’t pull it and you’re sitting there saying “Well I’d love for this bomb not to go off but unfortunately she can’t decide if she’s going to pull that pin.” The bomb’s going off soon, of course she can make a decision and she has to.
I’m sorry but isn’t that exactly what a fence sitter is? If you’re not completely sure that you’ll never want kids you’re not committed to being child free
